nodes.label: compose / First-Class Function Example
nodes.rationale: `compose = (f, g) -> x -> f(g(x))` demonstrates curried, function-returning-function syntax as the idiomatic Karl shape.

nodes.label: makeAdder Closure Example
nodes.rationale: Canonical demonstration of lexical capture (`makeAdder = n -> x -> n + x`) reused across REPL, notebook and docs.

nodes.label: Loop-as-Expression (for ... with ... then)
nodes.rationale: Loops carry accumulator bindings via `with` and yield a value via `then`, with `break v` supplying an early result — so iteration composes as an expression instead of mutating outer state.

nodes.label: Match Expression with Guards Example
nodes.rationale: `case _ if n < 0 -> ...` shows guard clauses layered on wildcard patterns with a final catch-all arm.
